newsitem.title: USA: US semiconductor equipment April book-to-bill ratio at 1.13. [CORRECTED 21:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: US semiconductor equipment April book-to-bill ratio at 1.13. [CORRECTED 21:35 GMT]

text.p: The North American semiconductor equipment industry posted a book-to-bill ratio of 1.13 for April 1997, compared with the revised ratio of 1.18 for March 1997, according to an international trade association.
The ratio means that $113 in orders were received for each $100 worth of products shipped.

Semiconductor Equipment and Materials International (SEMI) said late on Friday that although the book-to-bill ratio for April was lower than that for March, total semiconductor equipment orders in April increased 9.2 percent from the prior month, to $1.42 billion.
The bookings figure was about four percent above April 1996, the association said.

Total semiconductor equipment shipped by North American suppliers in April 1997 rose about 13.6 percent above the March level to $1.25 billion, SEMI said. Shipments were about seven percent below April 1996 levels.
